'''Attila Szabo''' is a [[biophysicist]] who is a Distinguished Investigator and Section Chief of the Theoretical Biophysical Chemistry Section in the Laboratory of Chemical Physics at the [[National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases]], part of the United States [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name="niddk">{{cite web |title=Attila Szabo, Ph.D., NIH Distinguished Investigator |url=https://irp.nih.gov/pi/attila-szabo |website=National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases |accessdate=14 August 2018}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Szabo was born in [[Budapest, Hungary]] in 1947. His family left Hungary in response to the [[Hungarian Revolution of 1956]] - he later recalled a dramatic escape over the border to [[Austria]] - and immigrated to [[Canada]], settling in [[Montreal]].<ref name="szabo_2008">{{cite journal |last1=Szabo |first1=Attila |title=Autobiography of Attila Szabo |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B |date=May 2008 |volume=112 |issue=19 |pages=5883–5886 |doi=10.1021/jp800825t}}</ref> Interested in chemistry since he was a child, Szabo studied the subject at [[McGill University]] as an undergraduate and received his bachelor's degree in 1968.<ref name=niddk /><ref name=szabo_2008 /> He then began graduate school at [[Harvard University]], where he joined [[Martin Karplus]]' research group. There he was introduced to theoretical work on [[NMR spectroscopy]] and developed a [[statistical mechanics|statistical mechanical]] model of the [[hemoglobin]] [[protein]]. Szabo accompanied Karplus on a [[sabbatical]] in Paris in 1972, and then spent a year in Cambridge working jointly with [[A. David Buckingham|David Buckingham]] and [[Max Perutz]].<ref name=szabo_2008 /> Szabo received his Ph.D. from Harvard in 1973.<ref name=niddk />

==Academic career==
Szabo joined the faculty at the [[University of Indiana, Bloomington]] in 1974. NMR was an active area of research there at the time and Szabo became involved in developing theoretical models to interpret NMR studies of biomolecules. Among the resulting work on [[NMR relaxation]], the [[Lipari-Szabo model-free formalism]] for modeling the dynamics of molecules was most influential and remains in active use in the field.<ref name=szabo_2008 /><ref name="lipari_1982">{{cite journal |last1=Lipari |first1=Giovanni |last2=Szabo |first2=Attila |title=Model-free approach to the interpretation of nuclear magnetic resonance relaxation in macromolecules. 1. Theory and range of validity |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=August 1982 |volume=104 |issue=17 |pages=4546–4559 |doi=10.1021/ja00381a009|bibcode=1982JAChS.104.4546L }}</ref><ref name="eaton_2008">{{cite journal |last1=Eaton |first1=William |title=A Tribute to Attila Szabo |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B |date=May 2008 |volume=112 |issue=19 |pages=5881–5882 |doi=10.1021/jp801687s|pmid=18461907 |pmc=7307604 }}</ref> While at Indiana Szabo also co-authored a textbook on [[quantum chemistry]] with fellow Karplus lab member [[Neil Ostlund]].<ref name=szabo_2008 /><ref name=eaton_2008 />

In 1979, Szabo was informed that he had not received [[tenure]] at Indiana.<ref name=szabo_2008 /> As he later recalled, his Ph.D. advisor Karplus connected him with [[William Eaton (scientist)|Bill Eaton]] at the [[National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases]], who recruited Szabo to NIDDK.<ref name=szabo_2008 /> Szabo has remained at NIDDK since and is currently Section Chief of the Theoretical Biophysical Chemistry Section in the Laboratory of Chemical Physics. His research group currently works on developing theoretical models of [[single-molecule experiment]]s,<ref name=niddk /> including collaborations with [[Irina Gopich]] and [[Gerhard Hummer]].<ref name=szabo_2008 /><ref name=eaton_2008 /> Szabo was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2010.<ref name="nas">{{cite web |title=Attila Szabo |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/attila-szabo-7clse2/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=14 August 2018}}</ref>
